process_note: The sfnl-prompt-master skill is not available in this subagent, so the hunt ran without it under the searcher definition.
conviction_note: Q4 is pinned inside the company's own guide (implied Q4 adj EBITDA $369.5-379.5m), so the reaction turns on the formal FY27 guide from a new CEO against a preliminary 'flat vs ~$1.48bn'. Sector guide cuts and the company's own 'inflation at the high end, pricing in the back half' comment lean that guide down. A stock 30% off its high, two target cuts in November, and 11.9% of shares short at 8.4 days to cover lean the other way. The findings sum to -0.3 and the scaled number is -0.28 at p_up 48 and abs 7.0; the two measurements agree that there is no usable direction, while the move itself should be large (FY-guide prints went -7.2, +9.8 and -12.8).
bar: Company guide: FY26 adj EBITDA $1,560-1,570m less nine-month $1,190.5m implies Q4 $369.5-379.5m (midpoint $374.5m) against $425.4m in Q4 FY25 (LTM $1,615.9m less 9M $1,190.5m), from the Q3 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530950/000153095026000076/ex99-1q32026er.htm. Street EPS $1.66 on ~$1.98bn revenue comes from one source (Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-11-11, https://finviz.com/news/421343/post-holdings-faces-fy27-reckoning-as-egg-windfall-fades-and-deleveraging-takes-priority); no second estimate source was reachable (chartmill 403). FY27 bar: the company's preliminary 'generally flat vs ~$1.48bn comparable adj EBITDA' (same 8-K). The street's own FY27 EBITDA figure was not found.
positioning_check: FINRA via equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/post/short-interest): 2026-10-30 5,215,964 shares short, 8.37 days to cover (about 11.9% of 43.96m shares outstanding); 2026-10-15 5,685,232, 8.65 DTC; down from 6,408,651 on 2026-08-14. MarketBeat put 2026-05-29 at 16.9% of float. That is a crowded but covering short, and days to cover are high because volume fell. Skew: the baseline rejected the chain (ATM spread 102% of mid, 25d skew 80 vol points implausible, OI 218), so there is no usable directional statement from options. The put/call OI ratio is 0.88 on a tiny OI.

expectations.price_path: Baseline: 5d -0.24%, 20d -3.14%, -30.7% from the 52w high, +9.5% off the 52w low ($71.45). The stock closed $84.72 on 2026-11-06 (Fox Business, https://www.foxbusiness.com/quote?stockTicker=POST) and $79.43 at the seal, about -6% in the two weeks into the print. Earnings Whispers (2026-11-11) had it down 5.4% since the last report, trailing the S&P by about 4 points. No sector ETF comparison was sourced.
expectations.vs_targets: Spot $79.4 against a 2026 target average of about $97.7 (six targets) and a high of $121 (Evercore, 2026-08-07); low $79 (Wells Fargo Hold, 2026-10-05). Recent cuts: Stifel 125->100 on 2026-10-15, JPM 99->93 on 2026-11-09, Barclays $88 Buy on 2026-11-19. Source: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/post/ratings/. Sources disagree on some prior targets.
expectations.whisper_or_buyside_bar: Earnings Whispers whisper field blank (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/POST). The EW preview frames the test: reaffirm a flat FY27 off $1.48bn with a gentle foodservice landing and steady pet and cereal, or the compounder case breaks (https://finviz.com/news/421343/post-holdings-faces-fy27-reckoning-as-egg-windfall-fades-and-deleveraging-takes-priority, 2026-11-11). It calls sentiment 'slightly more bearish' than before the last report.
expectations.last_print: Q3 FY26 (2026-08-06): adj EPS $1.78 vs $1.63 consensus (beat), revenue $1.95bn vs $2.02bn (miss), FY26 narrowed and a preliminary flat FY27 vs a rebased $1.48bn; stock -12.79% (baseline). Source: https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/POST and the Q3 8-K.
expectations.real_bar: For the stock to rise, the formal FY27 adj EBITDA guide must center at or near $1.48bn (not a range centered below it) with foodservice at or above its $500m run rate, from a new CEO, and the debt-paydown pivot must not come with a weaker cash outlook.

next_guide.street_full_year: not found (FY27 street EBITDA not sourced; the company's preliminary flat vs ~$1.48bn is the de facto anchor per the EW preview)
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY26 adj EBITDA $1,560-1,570m; FY27 preliminary 'generally flat' vs comparable ~$1.48bn (Q3 8-K, 2026-08-06, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530950/000153095026000076/ex99-1q32026er.htm)
next_guide.basis: The company already rebased to $1.48bn in August and described the budget as under development. Inflation tracking at the high end, back-half-weighted pricing, an egg-price collapse and sector-wide guide cuts give downside risk to the range, and a new CEO's first guide raises that risk, so the most likely outcome is a range around $1.48bn whose midpoint may sit slightly below it.

findings.finding: Q4 is pinned by the company's own narrowed FY26 guide: $1,560-1,570m less 9M adj EBITDA of $1,190.5m implies Q4 $369.5-379.5m (-11 to -13% vs Q4 FY25's ~$425m). Q3 came in 'slightly ahead of expectations' on foodservice, so the reported quarter lands inside or slightly above a narrow range the market already holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 beat EPS by $0.15 and the stock fell 12.79% on the FY27 outlook; Q4 FY25 (2025-11-20) beat by $0.21 and fell 7.15% (https://seekingalpha.com/news/4524697-post-holdings-non-gaap-eps-of-2_09-beats-by-0_21-revenue-of-2_25b-in-line). Quarter beats have not been paid.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: a guide range only $10m wide one quarter out leaves little room. It is filed so the judges see that the quarter cannot carry the move; a $10m beat is about 0.6% of annual EBITDA.
findings.independence: Q1/Q2 adj EBITDA ($418.2m, $395.0m) from the Q1 and Q2 8-Ks (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1530950/000153095026000019/ex99-1q12026er.htm) confirm the 9M sum. Same company documents.

findings.finding: Shell egg prices collapsed during Post's Q4 (Jul-Sep): Cal-Maine's quarter to 2026-08-29 showed conventional egg ASP -59.3% and a $58.6m net loss, and it expects continued pressure. That speeds the fade of the ~$60m foodservice earnings above the $500m run rate and is the input to FY27 foodservice. It also eases the 'market-priced vs grain-based egg cost' gap that hurt Refrigerated Retail in Q3. Fall HPAI outbreaks (IL 0.93m birds on 10-19, CA 1.3m on 10-28, about 0.5% of the flock) are too small to reverse it.
findings.link: Same product and market: Post's Michael Foods (Foodservice, ~$140m Q3 EBITDA, about 37% of company EBITDA) sells egg products partly at market-indexed prices and buys outside eggs. Cal-Maine is the largest US shell-egg producer and its ASP is the market series.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Foodservice upside drove the Q1 FY26 raise (+9.77%, 2026-02-05); its 'normalisation' framing accompanied the -12.79% Q3 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Management already guides foodservice to a $500m run rate, so the direction is known. Not known is whether a deeper-than-modelled egg collapse puts FY27 foodservice below $500m. If the market had priced that, previews would cite a foodservice cut; the EW preview still frames a 'gentle landing'. The net is small because Refrigerated Retail gains on the cost side.
findings.independence: Fall HPAI outbreak sizes from Food Ingredients First (https://www.foodingredientsfirst.com/news/bird-flu-egg-chicken-prices), a different source. It cuts slightly the other way, toward firmer prices into FY27 Q1.

findings.finding: The formal FY27 guide is the swing factor and leans down. On the Q3 call (2026-08-07), management said inflation was tracking toward the high end of expectations, offsetting pricing was weighted to the back half of FY27, and the budget was 'under development'. A new CEO (Catoggio, from 2026-10-01) gives his first guide, and the preliminary view was 'generally flat' vs ~$1.48bn. A range centered below $1.48bn is the main downside; a reaffirmed $1.48bn midpoint is the upside case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide line moves this stock: the first FY26 guide (2025-11-20) -7.15%, the Q1 FY26 raise +9.77%, the preliminary FY27 flat/rebase -12.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is near its lows and targets are being cut (Barclays $88 on 11-19). But the August rebase was framed as the final reset and the preview's central case is a reaffirmed flat. A guide centered below $1.48bn is not the modelled case. If it were priced, estimate revisions would show FY27 EBITDA below $1.48bn, and none was found.
findings.independence: Q3 release text: 'budget remains under development'; Foodservice growth, pricing and productivity to offset inflation and volume softness (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530950/000153095026000076/ex99-1q32026er.htm). CEO change: https://uk.marketscreener.com/news/post-holdings-inc-announces-ceo-changes-ce7f5bdade8ff620. Both are company statements; the preview reads the same call.

findings.finding: Packaged-food peers who reported after Post's August call cut or soft-guided on cost inflation and weak volume: Kraft Heinz cut its adjusted operating income outlook to -10 to -12% (from -5 to -10%); PepsiCo cut 2026 core EPS growth to 1-2% on North American costs (2026-10-09); Conagra volumes -2.1% with the CEO calling consumers pressured; Hormel and Mondelez cut. General Mills reaffirmed on 2026-09-23 but with NA Retail organic sales -3%.
findings.link: Same US grocery channel and consumer, and the same cost inputs (freight, packaging, grains). Post Consumer Brands (cereal, pet, peanut butter) about 50% of sales sells into the same retailers. General Mills is Post's direct cereal and pet competitor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific history for peer read-through; the guide line itself has moved the stock 7-13%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced at the sector level. The open question is whether Post's FY27 inflation assumption, set in August before these cuts, is now too low. It is filed small as macro-to-company transmission Post has not confirmed.
findings.independence: Kraft Heinz/Hormel/Mondelez cuts: https://www.emarketer.com/content/kraft-heinz-hormel-mondelez-lower-outlook-as-consumers-cut-spending ; Conagra: https://www.thepoultrysite.com/news/2026/10/conagra-sales-decline-as-inflation-squeezes-consumers ; GIS: https://finviz.com/news/394595/general-mills-reports-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-outlook. Overlaps with the next-guide finding only in direction; these are different documents.

findings.finding: Expectations have been reset lower into the print: spot $79.4 is 30.7% below the 52w high and about 19% below the 2026 average target (~$97.7). The stock fell about 6% from $84.72 (11-06) to $79.4 (11-19), and analysts cut targets in the final two weeks (JPM 99->93 on 11-09, Barclays to $88 on 11-19, Stifel 125->100 on 10-15). A reaffirmed flat FY27 would clear a bar the market has already lowered.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When the bar was set low after a de-rating, the Q1 FY26 raise paid +9.77%; when the stock went in higher (Q3, avg buyback price ~$99), the beat was sold -12.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The finding is that the bar is lower than the August setup, which favours the upside asymmetrically if the guide is merely held. If the market expected a reaffirmation, the stock would not be making fresh lows into the print with targets being cut on the day.
findings.independence: Price on 11-06 from Fox Business (https://www.foxbusiness.com/quote?stockTicker=POST); the EW preview says 'down 5.4% since last report' and 'slightly more bearish' (https://finviz.com/news/421343/post-holdings-faces-fy27-reckoning-as-egg-windfall-fades-and-deleveraging-takes-priority).

findings.finding: Short interest is crowded but covering: 5.22m shares short on 2026-10-30 (about 11.9% of 43.96m shares, 8.37 days to cover) against 6.41m on 2026-08-14. With heavy buybacks having shrunk the float (~17% share-count reduction FY26 YTD), 8+ days to cover means a reaffirmed guide forces covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest was 16.9% of float in May 2026 into the Q3 print, which still fell 12.79%; the short was right on a guide disappointment.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not priced; it is a mechanism. If the shorts had already covered, days to cover would be falling with volume rising. Instead volume fell (ADV 623k) and DTC rose to 8.4, so any upside surprise meets a thin offer.
findings.independence: MarketBeat 2026-05-29: 6.59m short, 16.92% of float, 7.9 DTC (via search snippet of https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/POST/short-interest/). Buyback share-count reduction is in the Q3 8-K.

findings.finding: Capital return is turning off: after repurchasing 9.1m shares for $908.8m in 9M FY26 (avg $100.34), Post bought only 0.4m shares ($39.3m at $88.80) from quarter end to 08-05 and said it will emphasise debt reduction. Net leverage was 4.6x on 2026-06-30, rising as EBITDA normalises. Management said refinancing rates rose and that a lower refinancing-rate environment could alter its view. The buyback bid is gone and FY27 interest expense is up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The pivot was announced with Q3 (-12.79%) and is known; no separate history.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced since August. What remains is whether FY27 adj EPS guidance or commentary, now including higher interest on 2034/2036 notes at 6.25-6.5% with no buyback offset, disappoints EPS-based holders. The money buys deleveraging, not growth. Signed slightly negative for EPS, though it also lowers balance-sheet risk.
findings.independence: The 2036 notes at 6.50% and the 2034 add-on at 6.25% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1530950/000153095026000041/post-20260313.htm) confirm the higher refinancing cost. The EW preview notes the pivot.

findings.finding: The cereal category is improving while Post lags it: US cold cereal sales -0.5% over the 52 weeks to 2026-06-28 vs -1.5% in 2025 (WK Kellogg data), and General Mills' cereal share loss narrowed to -0.1pt in its Jun-Aug quarter. But Post's consumption was -4.7% in Q3 on lost Malt-O-Meal distribution and price-pack moves, and its cereal and granola volume was -5.5% ex-8th Avenue.
findings.link: Same category: Post, General Mills and WK Kellogg are the three largest US RTE cereal makers. Cereal is the core of Post Consumer Brands (~$974m Q3 sales including pet and 8th Avenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cereal volume has not been the line the stock moved on in the last three prints; guide and foodservice were.
findings.why_not_priced: A slower category decline supports the 'volume pressure' assumption in the flat FY27 guide. Post's own Malt-O-Meal distribution loss is self-inflicted and laps. Small, because Post underperforms the category it reads through from.
findings.independence: GIS Q1 FY27 call (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/general-mills-q1-earnings-call-highlights) gives a different source on the same category direction.

findings.finding: Pet food read-through is soft for dog: General Mills' North America Pet (quarter to 2026-08-30) was flat in sales, with cat up double digits and dog down high-single digits. Post's pet volumes were -7.8% in Q3 ex-8th Avenue, about 60% of the decline from value brands (9Lives), and its Nutrish relaunch fell short of the flat-to-growth goal for the quarter.
findings.link: Same category and channel: GIS Blue Buffalo competes with Post's Nutrish and Kibbles 'n Bits in US dry dog food. Post holds about 30% share of its pet segments per management.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pet weakness has been a recurring drag cited on the Q2 and Q3 calls; no isolated reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Known drag. A dog-food decline that persisted into Jul-Sep slightly raises the risk that pet cost savings (benefits in FY28) do not cover FY27. Small, net of the cereal and foodservice lines, which are larger.
findings.independence: Nutrish shortfall from the EW preview (https://finviz.com/news/421343/post-holdings-faces-fy27-reckoning-as-egg-windfall-fades-and-deleveraging-takes-priority); a different source.

outside_window.finding: Pet cost savings and the two peanut-butter plant closures deliver benefits in FY28, not in FY27 or this window.

baseline_tension: No usable skew; the run-up (-3.1% 20d, -30.7% off the high, about -6% since 11-06) and a crowded short both cut against the negative guide lean, which is why p_up sits at 48 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short, 11.9% of shares at 8.4 DTC): negatives shrunk once: next guide -1.5 -> -1.2, egg -0.5 -> -0.4, peer cuts -0.5 -> -0.4, capital -0.4 -> -0.3; p_up 47 -> 48.
Rule 6 (inside the guided range; EPS consensus single-sourced): the Q4 reported-quarter finding moved toward 0, +0.3 -> +0.2.
Rule 5 (macro-to-company proxy): the peer guide-cut finding was kept small and filed, not dropped; no size change beyond rule 7.
Rules 1-2 (reaction function: beats sold, the guide is the line): already reflected in the draft; nothing further changed.
